answer: Rate-proportional difficulty resists sybils: the compute each action demands rises with the actor's recent submission RATE, measured per funding-correlated source, so a steady honest agent pays a flat floor while a burst from one operator climbs a terrace of escalating cost. A signal of many rapid submissions — the sybil footprint — triggers violet-hot difficulty that a lone genuine participant never sees. Cost attaches to velocity, not identity count, so splitting a burst across many keys from one source raises the SHARED difficulty they all must pay.
